method: Deterministic summary of computed figures. No language model is used.
national: One Nation led national search interest in the week to 10 October, averaging 30.0 on Google's 0-100 scale, 7.7 times the next party (Labor). That is 72% of all search interest across the parties tracked.
One Nation rose the most on the previous week, up 11.1 points (+59%); the Greens fell furthest, down 3.1 points (-45%).

Searches for the Greens jumped to 18 on 30 September, 7.9 times the previous week's average. Coverage around that day: “New Australian Greens leader David Shoebridge vows to ‘replace’ Labor” (Politico).
Fastest-rising searches alongside One Nation: “one nation candidates”, “one nation victoria”, “one nation leader”.
victoria: 47 days until Victorians vote on Saturday 28 November 2026.

Across the latest poll from each of 4 pollsters, the Coalition averages 29.2% of the primary vote, Labor 24.5%, One Nation 22.2% and the Greens 14.0%. On two-party-preferred the Coalition leads 53.7 to 46.3 (3 polls), an 8.7-point swing to the Coalition since 2022.
Applied uniformly to the 2022 pendulum, that swing points to a Coalition majority (50 seats, 45 needed). Treat this as the classic two-party read only: it cannot see One Nation winning seats.
The Roy Morgan MRP (March 2026 - September 2026), which models seats one by one, projects Coalition 62, Labor 40, One Nation 11 and Greens 6: a majority.
Preferred premier (Freshwater, 24–28 Sep 2026): Wilson 37%, Carroll 30%, Pickering 13%.
